title.narrative: Child project of the Global clean hydrogen programme for Nigeria

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The Nigeria Child Project of the GCHP aims to contribute to the overall goal and impact of the programme alongside the other national child projects, working in a coordinated manner under the guidance of the Global Child Project. The activities envisaged for the Nigeria Child Project will support the country’s energy transition by fostering the adoption of clean hydrogen technologies while delivering wide-ranging socio-economic benefits across key target sectors.The socio-economic benefits of the Nigeria Child Project include:· Capacity building and job creation: By conducting capacity-building activities and awareness-raising through national events and workshops, as well as through participation in thematic working groups, e-training sessions, and the Global Knowledge Platform managed by the Global Child Project, stakeholders in Nigeria will enhance their technical skills and expertise for developing the clean hydrogen market. These efforts will contribute to the creation of skilled jobs and elevate the quality of technical services offered by professionals in sectors linked to hydrogen production, infrastructure development, and technology management. Through knowledge dissemination and best practices, the project will support local industries in developing a skilled workforce required to sustain long-term growth in the clean hydrogen economy.· Innovation and industrial development: The Nigeria Child Project will promote technological innovation by fostering collaboration among industry stakeholders, international experts, and local governments. This collaboration will support strategic planning for green hydrogen implementation within industrial clusters and companies. By participating in the Global Knowledge Platform, Nigeria will benefit from shared best practices, innovation case studies, and south-south cooperation, spurring the development of hydrogen-related technologies and industries. This will open up economic opportunities in industrial and transport sectors, positioning Nigeria and its industries as leaders in the emerging green hydrogen economy. Such developments will generate direct and indirect jobs, driving socio-economic progress across the country.· Energy security and economic resilience: By focusing on clean hydrogen, the Nigeria Child Project will strengthen energy security by supporting the development of locally produced hydrogen as a reliable alternative to fossil fuels. This transition will reduce dependence on carbon-intensive energy sources, mitigate carbon emissions, and diversify job opportunities, making the national economy more resilient to global energy market shifts. Enhanced energy diversification will strengthen Nigeria’s energy systems, better meeting domestic energy demands and ensuring a sustainable and secure energy future.· Gender inclusion and social equity: The Nigeria Child Project will actively promote gender inclusion by ensuring women and youth are meaningfully involved in all project activities. The project will target 50% female participation and 20% youth participation in relevant activities, creating new opportunities for underrepresented groups in the clean hydrogen sector. Gender-responsive knowledge products will support social equity by offering equal access to employment opportunities and ensuring that the green hydrogen transition’s benefits are shared across communities.· Health and environmental benefits: By encouraging the adoption of clean hydrogen technologies, the Nigeria Child Project will reduce air pollution in industrial and urban areas, contributing to improved public health. The shift away from fossil fuels will lower harmful emissions, improving air quality and reducing pollution-related health risks. The project will also deliver environmental benefits through significant greenhouse gas emission reductions, helping Nigeria meet its net-zero or low-carbon development commitments while fostering healthier environments for its population. · Knowledge management and sharing: The Global Knowledge Platform created by the Global Child Project, alongside local knowledge products developed in Nigeria, will enable continuous learning and access to the latest research, best practices, and technological advancements in clean hydrogen. This knowledge-sharing ecosystem will build Nigeria’s capacity to innovate and implement hydrogen technologies while establishing a global network of practitioners. The socio-economic benefits of this knowledge-sharing process will extend beyond the project’s lifespan, ensuring sustainable and lasting impacts at both national and international levels.
